## Analyzing $g(u) = f(u)$ for $u \geq 0$

Computing $g(u) = ||u-2|-1|$ piecewise:

- $u \in [0,1]$: $g = 1-u$ (slope $-1$)
- $u \in [1,2]$: $g = u-1$ (slope $+1$)
- $u \in [2,3]$: $g = 3-u$ (slope $-1$)
- $u \in [3,4]$: $g = u-3$ (slope $+1$)

This is a triangular wave on $[0,4]$ oscillating between $0$ and $1$. Since $g(u)+g(v)=1$ requires both terms in $[0,1]$, we need $u,v \in [0,4]$.

## Symmetry reduction

The equation depends only on $|x|$ and $|y|$, giving 4-fold symmetry. I compute the curve in the first quadrant ($u=x\geq 0$, $v=y\geq 0$) with $g(u)+g(v)=1$, then multiply by 4.

## Line segments in each grid rectangle

The breakpoints at $u,v \in \{0,1,2,3,4\}$ create a $4\times 4$ grid of rectangles. In each, $g$ is linear in both variables, so the level set is a line segment. I verify all 16:

| $[1,2]\times[1,2]$ | $u-1,\;v-1$ | $u+v=3$ | $(1,2)\to(2,1)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[1,2]\times[2,3]$ | $u-1,\;3-v$ | $v=u+1$ | $(1,2)\to(2,3)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[1,2]\times[3,4]$ | $u-1,\;v-3$ | $u+v=5$ | $(1,4)\to(2,3)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[2,3]\times[0,1]$ | $3-u,\;1-v$ | $u+v=3$ | $(2,1)\to(3,0)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[2,3]\times[1,2]$ | $3-u,\;v-1$ | $v=u-1$ | $(2,1)\to(3,2)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[2,3]\times[2,3]$ | $3-u,\;3-v$ | $u+v=5$ | $(2,3)\to(3,2)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[2,3]\times[3,4]$ | $3-u,\;v-3$ | $v=u+1$ | $(2,3)\to(3,4)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[3,4]\times[0,1]$ | $u-3,\;1-v$ | $v=u-3$ | $(3,0)\to(4,1)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[3,4]\times[1,2]$ | $u-3,\;v-1$ | $u+v=5$ | $(3,2)\to(4,1)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |
| $[3,4]\times[2,3]$ | $u-3,\;3-v$ | $v=u-1$ | $(3,2)\to(4,3)$ | $\sqrt{2}$ |

Every segment has slope $\pm 1$ with run $1$ and rise $1$, so each has length $\sqrt{2}$. All 16 rectangles contribute exactly one full segment (endpoints lie on the rectangle boundary as verified).

So $a = 64$, $b = 2$ (squarefree), and

$$a + b = 64 + 2 = \boxed{66}$$
